official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 Part L publication
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Document L 2026 was published on 24 March 2026 for England.

official_measurement_examples.name: Future effective date
official_measurement_examples.fact: Circular 01/2026 says the new approvals generally take effect on 24 March 2027 and later for specified HRB work, subject to transitions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current SAP method
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Standard Assessment Procedure page updated 8 June 2026 says SAP 10.3 is currently the sole approved methodology for Future Homes Standard compliance calculations.

official_measurement_examples.name: HEM delay
official_measurement_examples.fact: The same June 2026 update states the Home Energy Model launch was delayed and had not launched alongside the Future Homes Standard.

official_measurement_examples.name: Earlier Part L standards
official_measurement_examples.fact: Earlier Approved Document L versions continue to matter for projects falling within previous regulatory standards and transition rules.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 dwelling statistics
official_measurement_examples.fact: Official statistics published in 2026 monitor new dwellings built to the Part L 2021 standard and are not parcel-level energy compliance certificates.

official_measurement_examples.name: Impact assessment caveat
official_measurement_examples.fact: The RPC's 2026 red rating concerns the quality of the impact-assessment evidence and does not invalidate the policy itself.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Part L compliance and energy modelling do not themselves grant planning permission or reserve utility capacity.

core_rules: Part L compliance is not planning permission
planning permission is not Part L compliance
2026 Approved Document L must not be treated as generally effective before its stated 2027 date
SAP 10.3 current approval must not be replaced by an unlaunched HEM
HEM consultation material is not an operative compliance methodology
energy model output is not a utility connection offer
EPC data is not parcel planning permission
national dwelling statistics are not individual parcel facts
earlier Part L standards remain relevant under transition rules
impact assessment is not building-control approval
RPC opinion on evidence is not policy revocation
compliance guide is not proof of as-built performance
energy target is not parcel development capacity
Part L compliance does not create ownership or access rights
no parcel energy clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
